I do not think we have met. Claire Bennett, I teach on this programme. And you are?
Eduardo Alves. I am a lawyer, from Sao Paulo.
A lawyer covers a lot of ground. What do you do, exactly?
I advise companies that buy and sell grain. Corn and sugar, mostly, and a few clients who import diesel.
So you spend your week in court?
No, we do not go to a hearing every week. We write contracts and we read the ones the other side sends. I am a partner, so I answer for that work.
Good. That is exactly what we read in this course: contracts, in English. So why this programme, and why now?
Because the contract is in English and the client is not. And you — what do you teach here?
I am a partner, and our firm has an office in Sao Paulo and one in Miami.

Good afternoon, Eduardo. This is Claire Bennett from the programme office. I teach the Monday group. We start on the ninth of March, at seven in the evening, in room 204. We meet twice a week, on Monday and on Thursday. In the first class you introduce yourself. You say your name, you say what you practise, and you say why you are here. Two minutes, no more. Please bring your passport and one photo. My number is 21 4470 8890. Thank you, Eduardo.

Hello, Eduardo. My name is Tom Baker. I work for Harrow Shipping in London. I advise grain traders on their contracts, and we import corn and soya from Brazil every month. We have a meeting on Thursday, at ten o'clock, London time. I send you the papers today. We need two things from you: the name of your law firm, and one page about your work. The deadline is Wednesday at six. You have my number. Thank you, and see you on Thursday.

Eduardo, this is Claire again. One more thing about the first week. We read one contract in every class, and you choose it. I need your contract before Friday. Please send me one page, in English, about a real shipment: the product, the country, and the price. We do not need the name of the client. We use the page only in class. Twelve people are in the group this term, and we read twelve different contracts. That is the whole course. Thank you.
